target.title: feat(exec): deny-over-allow exec approval denylist (#6615)
target.body:
Fixes #6615. Supersedes #92456 (author inactive since 2026-06-12, no response to review, conflicts with main — full credit to @Hidetsugu55 for the STOP-list concept and dual-host enforcement approach, both kept here).

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's exec approvals support allowlists but no denylist: there is no way to force human approval (or denial) for specific dangerous commands when an agent runs at `security=full` / `ask=off`, or when a broad allowlist/durable trust would otherwise auto-approve them. #6615 asks for a deny-over-allow screening layer so commands like `git push --force` or `rm -rf` patterns always require an explicit human decision, regardless of permissive settings.

## Fix

- New `src/infra/exec-approvals-denylist.ts`: entry normalization, strict validation (`collectExecDenylistErrors`), and `resolveEffectiveExecDenylist` (de-duplicated union across layers — deny anywhere = deny).
- **Both config layers**, unlike #92456: `openclaw.json` `tools.exec.denylist` (global + per-agent) **and** `~/.openclaw/exec-approvals.json` (defaults + `*` + agent).
- **Shared pattern language**: denylist patterns reuse the existing allowlist glob compiler via a new `matchesExecGlob` export — no second matcher to keep in sync.
- **Deny wins first**: `requiresExecApproval({ denylisted })` short-circuits ahead of `ask=off`, `security=full`, allowlist hits, and durable allow-always trust, in the single decision function both the gateway exec host and node-host `system.run` policy already call (node denial reason: `denylist-hit`). Explicit allow-once approval still clears a hit; `security=deny` still wins overall.
- Conservative fallback kept from #92456: unanalyzable command + configured denylist ⇒ approval required, not fail-open. Basename variants and `bash -c "..."` inner payloads are screened.

## Evidence

**Focused tests: 38 passing** (`exec-approvals-denylist.test.ts` 19 new; `exec-policy.test.ts` 19 incl. 6 new): exact-command deny, glob deny, basename + wrapper payload, deny-beats-allowlist, deny-beats-ask-off/full-security, deny-beats-durable-trust, both-layer union, malformed-entry validation, conservative fallback, security=deny precedence, approval-clears vs durable-trust-does-not.

**Typecheck**: `tsc -p tsconfig.core.json --noEmit` on this branch reports no errors beyond the one pre-existing `src/secrets/config-io.ts` TS4058 already present on current `main` (verified against `origin/main` baseline on the same machine).

**Real behavior proof** (real decision code path via `node --import tsx`, no test doubles — `git push --force origin main` allowlisted + durable-trusted at `security=full`/`ask=off`):

```
## BEFORE (control: no denylist configured)
[gateway-host] command="git push --force origin main" security=full ask=off allowlisted=true durable=true -> AUTO-RUN
[node-host]    command="git push --force origin main" -> ALLOWED

## AFTER (denylist configured via openclaw.json tools.exec.denylist)
denylist = [{"pattern":"git push*--force*","reason":"history rewrite"}]
[gateway-host] -> APPROVAL REQUIRED
[node-host]    -> DENIED (denylist-hit)

## AFTER + explicit allow-once approval
[node-host]    -> ALLOWED (approval cleared the hit)
```

## Scope notes

- Diff kept tight: +645/−4 across 8 files; no drive-by refactors.
- Follow-up candidates (intentionally out of this diff): wiring `collectExecDenylistErrors` into the top-level `openclaw config validate` pass, and threading the openclaw.json layer union at the gateway host caller (resolver + param already in place).


**Full repo validation** (post-review fixes, head `1a42527cf0d`): `CI=1 pnpm check:changed` full heavy lane — **exit 0**: typecheck all, oxlint core/extensions/scripts (0 errors), runtime import cycles, and all repo guards pass.
